text:
maya: Heads up — I patched the frontend Service in cluster to add an external-dns hostname and now `terraform plan` wants to replace the Service and the DNS record. Did I just break state? :grimacing:

sam: which annotation exactly? external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/hostname?

maya: yep, added `external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/hostname: app.blue.example.com` so we can test the blue cluster. quick and dirty patch via kubectl.

alex: can you paste the plan snippet? usually that indicates drift or an orphaned DNS record in cloud provider.

maya: paste of the relevant lines from plan:```
-/+ kubernetes_service.frontend (server will be replaced)
  ~ metadata.annotations: "..." => "..."
-/+ google_dns_record_set.app (replaced)
  id: "-" => "app.blue.example.com.A."
```

chun: sounds like the external-dns controller wrote a record in Cloud DNS (or the cloud provider created an LB) that isn't in Terraform state. If TF didn't manage that record before, plan will try to create/replace.

alex: two quick checks: is the remote state locked? sometimes pipeline applies hold the lock and a stuck run prevents imports. run `terraform state pull | jq .` or check S3 lock metadata.

ops-bot: remote state backend: s3://redwood-tf/infra-state is currently LOCKED by run id `ci-24-apply` (owner: sam) since 1758995000.

sam: that was my pipeline earlier — it should have finished, maybe the lock didn't clear. if it's still held and no apply is running we can `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>` after confirming.

alex: recommended sequence (from least to most intrusive):
1) confirm no active apply (CI + ops)
2) run `terraform import kubernetes_service.frontend default/frontend` to bring the actual service into state
3) import the dns record set if the cloud record exists: `terraform import google_dns_record_set.app "projects/myproj/managedZones/examplezonesets_app/A/app.blue.example.com"`
4) `terraform plan` again

commands to try:```bash
# unlock if stuck (only after confirming no apply)
terraform force-unlock 1c2d3e4f
# import k8s svc into state
terraform import kubernetes_service.frontend default/frontend
# import dns record (example)
terraform import google_dns_record_set.app projects/myproj/managedZones/example-zone/A/app.blue.example.com
```

maya: I can't run import, the backend says locked. getting `Error: The state file is locked by: ci-24-apply`

sam: I'll check CI and force-unlock if it's stale. stand by.

(5m)
sam: I did a force-unlock from my dev shell — lock id was stale. maya you should be able to run imports now.

maya: import of the k8s svc succeeded, then imported the DNS record. ran `terraform plan` and the replace is gone. phew.

alex: root cause: manual kubectl patch + external-dns controller created/updated provider-managed DNS outside of Terraform; terraform state had no record for it so plan wanted to create/replace. Importing both cluster svc and DNS record reconciled state.

chun: action items:
- maya to add a short note in ops playbooks about annotating via terraform manifests or flagging changes before kubectl patching
- infra to add a tiny runbook for stuck S3 locks (how to verify and force-unlock safely)

maya: will add the note and ping infra in a follow-up PR. thanks for the quick help everyone :tada:

ops-bot: reminder: consider adding a CI check that flags direct kubectl edits to critical services (optional).
